argv:
Rewrite the text following Google's developer documentation style.

Write in the second person and the present tense. Use the active voice and
standard American spelling. Keep the tone precise and even-handed rather than
casual — this is documentation, not conversation. Write complete sentences;
do not use fragments for effect, and do not use contractions.

Prefer short sentences and short paragraphs. Use a numbered list for a
sequence of steps and a bulleted list for an unordered set. Begin each list
item with a capital letter.

Avoid the words "simply", "easily", "just", "obviously", and "of course": what
is obvious to the writer is rarely obvious to the reader. Do not use
placeholder words like "please" in instructions. Avoid metaphors, idioms, and
cultural references that will not translate, and avoid asides or personality
that could distract a reader who is scanning for an answer.

Use inclusive, unambiguous language and spell out an abbreviation on first
use. When in doubt, prefer the more explicit and fully spelled-out phrasing
over the more familiar-sounding one.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
The Millbrook Hollow City Council voted Tuesday night to approve an amended version of the parks and recreation line item, following a meeting that also touched on the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge. According to a spokesperson for the mayor's office, the revised figure reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members, though the spokesperson declined to characterize those conversations further. A separate memo, attributed by two council staffers to the finance subcommittee, put the adjustment at approximately $340,000, a figure that a budget analyst who reviewed the memo said was "in the range we expected." Buried near the end of that same memo, and not raised by any council member during the meeting, was a line noting that the bridge's lead structural engineer had flagged a load-bearing crack serious enough to warrant closing the span to truck traffic within 90 days. The bridge project, which has appeared on the capital plan since at least 2019 and has already drawn 14 change orders, was not discussed in detail. Council member Dana Okafor, reached after the meeting, said only that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
</passage>

response.text:
On Tuesday night, the Millbrook Hollow City Council voted to approve an amended version of the parks and recreation line item. The meeting also addressed the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge.

A spokesperson for the mayor's office says the revised figure reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members. The spokesperson did not provide further detail about those conversations.

Two council staffers attribute a separate memo to the finance subcommittee. The memo puts the adjustment at approximately $340,000. A budget analyst who reviewed the memo describes this figure as "in the range we expected."

Near the end of the same memo is a line that no council member raised during the meeting. The line states that the bridge's lead structural engineer flagged a load-bearing crack serious enough to warrant closing the span to truck traffic within 90 days.

The bridge project has appeared on the capital plan since at least 2019 and has already drawn 14 change orders. The council did not discuss the project in detail.

Council member Dana Okafor, reached after the meeting, said only that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
